rejected.statement: Futalognkosaurus is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur whose name means "giant chief lizard".
rejected.quote: Futalognkosaurus ( ; meaning "giant chief lizard") is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur.

rejected.statement: The herbivorous Futalognkosaurus lived between 93.5 and 85.8 million years ago in the Portezuelo Formation of Argentina during the Coniacian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: The herbivorous Futalognkosaurus lived approximately 93.5 to 85.8 million years ago in the Portezuelo Formation, in what is now Argentina, of the Coniacian stage of the late Cretaceous Period.

rejected.statement: Fossil evidence from the site suggests Futalognkosaurus lived in a warm, tropical climate in Patagonia.
rejected.quote: The fish and fossilized leaf debris on the site, together with other dinosaur remains, suggest a warm tropical climate in Patagonia during this period.

rejected.statement: Fossils of Futalognkosaurus were discovered in Neuquén province, Argentina, in 2000 and scientifically described in 2007.
rejected.quote: Fossils of Futalognkosaurus were found in the Neuquén province of Argentina in 2000, and were scientifically described in 2007.

rejected.statement: Researchers hypothesize that the holotype specimen was washed into a river near its death margins.
rejected.quote: The holotype was found near the margins of a river. The holotype was hypothesised to have been washed into the river after its death.

rejected.statement: The giant carcass likely acted as a river barrier long enough to create an oxbow lake where fish and bivalves lived.
rejected.quote: Due to its giant size the carcass likely acted as a barrier, altering the course of the river around it, lasting long enough for fish and bivalves to live in it, and eventually leaving an oxbow lake behind.

rejected.statement: The genus is based on three fossil specimens that yield an estimated 70% of the skeleton.
rejected.quote: It is based on three fossil specimens, yielding an estimated 70% of the skeleton in total.

rejected.statement: The discovery team described the find as the most complete giant dinosaur known at the time.
rejected.quote: The fossil team described the find as "the most complete giant dinosaur known so far".

rejected.statement: Futalognkosaurus had a long neck with 14 vertebrae that was over a meter deep in places due to tall neural spines shaped like shark fins.
rejected.quote: Its long neck contained 14 vertebrae, and was over a meter deep in places due to its extremely tall neural spines which had a distinctive "shark-fin" shape.

rejected.statement: The hips of Futalognkosaurus were extremely large and bulky, reaching a width of nearly 3 meters.
rejected.quote: The hips were also extremely large and bulky, reaching a width of nearly 3 m.

rejected.statement: Futalognkosaurus is an enormous sauropod with a long tail, long neck, and giant body.
rejected.quote: El Futalognkosaurus es un saurópodo enorme con cola larga, cuello largo y cuerpo gigante.

rejected.statement: The type species Futalognkosaurus dukei is estimated to be 26 to 30 meters long and weigh 38 to 50 tonnes.
rejected.quote: La especie tipo, Futalognkosaurus dukei, se estima con una longitud de 26 a 30 metros y un peso de 38 a 50 toneladas.

rejected.statement: Three very complete specimens were recovered, consisting of one adult and two juveniles.
rejected.quote: Se rescataron tres ejemplares muy completos, un adulto y dos juveniles.

rejected.statement: The genus name comes from the Mapudungun language of the Mapuche people, where "futa" means "giant" and "lognko" means "chief".
rejected.quote: El nombre del género proviene de la lengua de los mapuches, etnia que habita la zona, Mapudungun "futa" que significa "gigante" y "lognko" "jefe".

rejected.statement: Calvo and colleagues classified Futalognkosaurus as a member of Titanosauridae or Lithostrotia, most closely related to Mendozasaurus.
rejected.quote: In their phylogenetic analysis, Calvo and colleagues found Futalognkosaurus to be a member of the Titanosauridae (or Lithostrotia, depending on the definitions being used), and most closely related to Mendozasaurus.

rejected.statement: Researchers defined a new clade called Lognkosauria containing Futalognkosaurus, Mendozasaurus, their common ancestor, and all descendants.
rejected.quote: They defined a new clade for the group containing both Futalognkosaurus and Mendozasaurus, their common ancestor, and all descendants, which they named the Lognkosauria.

rejected.statement: A new clade named Lognkosauria was defined to contain Futalognkosaurus, Mendozasaurus, their common ancestor, and all descendants.
rejected.quote: De esta manera definen un nuevo clado que contiene a Futalognkosaurus y Mendozasaurus, su ancestro común y todos sus descendientes, al que llamaron Lognkosauria.

rejected.statement: Authors found that Malawisaurus belonged to a sister group of the Lognkosauria clade.
rejected.quote: Los autores encontraron que Malawisaurus debió pertenecer a u grupo hermano de este clado.

rejected.statement: It is believed these titanosauroids lived about 87 million years ago in a humid environment abundant with lakes and lagoons.
rejected.quote: Se cree que estos titanosauroides vivieron hace unos 87 millones de años en un ambiente húmedo en el que abundaban lagos y lagunas con una gran variedad biológica.

rejected.statement: It is probable that, like other sauropods, Futalognkosaurus exhibited gregarious behavior to increase safety against predators like Megaraptor.
rejected.quote: Probablemente, como todos los saurópodos, tenía algún comportamiento del tipo gregario que les permitía tener una mayor seguridad ante los depredadores de su ecosistema, como el megarráptor.

rejected.statement: The time range for Futalognkosaurus is recorded as Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago).
rejected.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The estimated length of Futalognkosaurus was revised downward to 26 meters in 2008.
rejected.quote: In 2008 this was downsized to 26 m.

rejected.statement: The genus is based on three fossil specimens that together provide 70% of the skeleton.
rejected.quote: Está basado en restos fósiles de tres especímenes, que juntos brindan el 70% del esqueleto.
